messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.reasoning: We need to calculate entropy change for heating ice from 0°C to 100°C under 1 atm. But we have a 1 kg ice block at 0°C. Heating to 100°C under 1 atm. But ice at 0°C melting at 1 atm. So process: ice at 0°C -> melt at 0°C -> water at 0°C -> heat water to 100°C. Also water at 100°C under 1 atm will boil to steam at 100°C. But question says heated to 100°C under 1 atm. That implies final state is water at 100°C? Or steam? Usually heating ice to 100°C under 1 atm means final state is steam at 100°C. But they didn't mention boiling. But typical scenario: ice at 0°C -> water at 0°C -> steam at 100°C. But they might want to include phase change. Let's interpret as final state is steam at 100°C. So we need to compute entropy change for each step: melting, heating water, vaporization. Use standard entropies: S°(ice) at 0°C, S°(water) at 0°C, S°(steam) at 100°C. But we can compute using enthalpy changes and temperatures. For phase changes at constant T, ΔS = ΔH/T. For heating water from 0°C to 100°C, ΔS = ∫ Cp dT / T. Use Cp of water ~ 4.18 kJ/kg·K. For steam heating from 0°C to 100°C? Actually steam at 100°C is saturated steam at 1 atm. But we don't need heating steam because final state is steam at 100°C. So steps: ice at 0°C -> water at 0°C: ΔS1 = ΔH_fus / T_melt. ΔH_fus of ice at 0°C is 6.01 kJ/kg. So ΔS1 = 6.01 kJ/kg / 273.15 K = 0.0220 kJ/kg·K = 22 J/kg·K. Next: water at 0°C -> water at 100°C: ΔS2 = ∫ Cp_water dT / T. Cp_water ~ 4.18 kJ/kg·K. So ΔS2 = 4.18 kJ/kg·K * ln(373.15/273.15). ln ratio = ln(373.15/273.15)=ln(1.366)=0.312. So ΔS2 = 4.18*0.312=1.305 kJ/kg·K = 1305 J/kg·K. Next: water at 100°C -> steam at 100°C: ΔS3 = ΔH_vap / T_boil. ΔH_vap of water at 100°C is 40.79 kJ/kg. So ΔS3 = 40.79 kJ/kg / 373.15 K = 0.1093 kJ/kg·K = 109.3 J/kg·K. Sum ΔS_total = 22 + 1305 + 109.3 = 1436.3 J/kg·K. For 1 kg, same. So answer ~ 1440 J/K. But we need to use tool.
